failure_summary.description: Model defaults to the most prominent associated entity (title/category) instead of resolving the specific semantic slot requested (author/specific member).

patch.reasoning: Both failures stem from the model matching on surface-level prominence (poem title, regional category) rather than identifying the precise semantic role demanded by the clue (author, specific country). Adding a rule to explicitly distinguish source vs. creator and category vs. member will force slot verification before extraction.

edits.target: - **Handle Fragments, Ellipses & Appositives**: Questions often contain trailing ellipses (`...`), cut-off syntax, or standalone noun phrases/titles. Ignore non-semantic noise and focus on core identifying constraints. Additionally, treat descriptive phrases or appositives (e.g., 'this South American capital') as primary search anchors to locate candidate entities.
edits.content: - **Distinguish Source vs. Creator & Category vs. Member**: When clues reference works, quotes, lists, or categories, explicitly determine whether the question targets the originator (author/creator), the specific work/title, or a particular member. Avoid defaulting to the most visually prominent match (e.g., poem title, region name) if the clue's intent points to the creator or a specific instance. Verify the required semantic slot before extraction.
